Definition: A button that shows a color. Pressing it opens a color picker to choose a new color.
The panel a color well opens. It has a hue ring, a saturation and brightness square, red, green and blue sliders, a hex field, 16 swatches, and Cancel and OK buttons.
A color written as a pound sign and six hex digits, such as #2F5BBB. The first two digits are the red, the next two the green and the last two the blue, each from 00 to FF.
Where a color sits around the color wheel, from 0 to 360 degrees. Red is at 0, green at 120 and blue at 240.
A small square of one ready-made color that a person can pick with one click or key.
A number from 1 to 21 that says how different two colors look in lightness. Text is easier to read when the contrast with its background is higher.
An object that a control tells when something happens. A ColorWellListener is told when a person changes a color well's color.
